'''Joshua O'Neal Jackson''' (born February 10, 1997) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player He played [[college basketball]] for one season with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] before declaring for the [[2017 NBA draft]], where he was selected fourth overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. ==Early life== Jackson was born in [[San Diego County, California]] while his mother, Apples Jones, was serving in the [[U.S. Navy]] and lived there until he was eight months old when she moved them to [[Detroit]] to be closer to her family.{{Cite web |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7142 |title=Josh Jackson Profile |website=University of Kansas Athletics Department |date=April 14, 2016 |access-date=June 15, 2017}}{{cite news |last=Roberts |first=Ben |url=http://www.kentucky.com/2014/07/20/3344822/star-recruits-mom-says-hes-not.html |title=Star recruit's mom says he's not being recruited |newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=July 20, 2014 |access-date=April 4, 2016 |archive-date=September 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920174553/http://www.kentucky.com/2014/07/20/3344822/star-recruits-mom-says-hes-not.html |url-status=dead }} In the eighth grade, he was held back a grade due to his passion for basketball overtaking his grades, with Jackson going to Voyager Middle School for his repeated year before entering high school.{{Cite news|url=http://heavy.com/news/2017/06/josh-jackson-family-bio-age-parents-mom-nba-draft/|title=Josh Jackson's Family: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know|last=Levine|first=Daniel S.|date=June 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625133609/http://heavy.com/news/2017/06/josh-jackson-family-bio-age-parents-mom-nba-draft/|url-status=dead}} He attended Consortium College Prep School in Detroit his freshman and sophomore years, before moving to [[Napa, California]] to attend [[Justin-Siena High School]] for his junior and senior year. ==High school career== [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Josh Jackson at the rim.jpg|thumb|Jackson drives to the basket in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]].|alt=]] As a freshman for the Consortium College Prep School, Jackson averaged 17 [[Point (basketball)|points]], six [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], four [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] and four [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game.{{cite web |date=April 4, 2013 |title=Metro Detroit boys and girls basketball Freshman of the Year: Josh Jackson and Bailey Thomas are future stars - MLive.com |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/metro-detroit-boys-and-girls-basketball-freshman-of-the-year-josh-jackson-and-bailey-thomas-are-future-stars/ |access-date=October 5, 2024 |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com}} As a sophomore, he led the school to their first state title.{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/649699779975320672/josh-jackson-leads-detroit-consortium-basketball-to-first-class-c-title-breaks-silence-to-share-season-of-joy/ |title=Josh Jackson leads Detroit Consortium basketball to first Class C title, breaks silence to share season of joy - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date=March 23, 2014 |access-date=April 6, 2016}} He averaged 28 points, 15 rebounds and six assists per game.{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/2977845755363436201/josh-jackson-of-detroit-consortium-is-2014-mlive-detroit-player-of-the-year-for-boys-basketball/ |title=Josh Jackson of Detroit Consortium is 2014 MLive Detroit Player of the Year for boys basketball - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date=April 11, 2014 |access-date=April 6, 2016}} Prior to his junior year, Jackson and his family moved to California to attend [[Justin-Siena High School]] in [[Napa, California]] and play for [[Prolific Prep]].{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/3889361316306006313/josh-jackson-announces-transfer-to-justin-siena-a-catholic-prep-school-in-california/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820142125/http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/3889361316306006313/josh-jackson-announces-transfer-to-justin-siena-a-catholic-prep-school-in-california/ |title=Josh Jackson announces transfer to Justin-Siena, a Catholic prep school in California - MLive.com |website=Highschoolsports.mlive.com |date=August 2014 |access-date=April 6, 2016 |archive-date=August 20, 2014|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://archive.freep.com/article/20140726/HSS/307260040/Shawn-Windsor-Detroit-Prep-star-Josh-Jackson-is-chasing-his-dream-in-California |title=Detroit Free Press - Home |website=Archive.freep.com |access-date=April 6, 2016}}{{cite web|last=Sernoffsky |first=Evan |url=http://www.sfgate.com/education/article/Basketball-star-headed-to-Napa-school-that-5658223.php |title=Basketball star headed to Napa school that doesn't yet exist |publisher=SFGate |date=July 31, 2014 |access-date=April 6, 2016}} As a Junior, he averaged 31.2 [[points per game]] and 5.4 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]]. As a Senior, Jackson averaged 26.9 points and 13.1 [[rebounds per game]]. Jackson played AAU basketball for 1Nation Elite, a program founded by his mother. In March 2016, Jackson, played in the 2016 [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and led in scoring with 19 points, whilst also recording four rebounds and three assists. He was named co-MVP alongside [[Frank Jackson (basketball)|Frank Jackson]].{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/josh-jackson-does-some-of-everything-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game-win|title=Co-MVP Josh Jackson does some of everything in McDonald's All American Game win|website=USA Today High School Sports|date=March 31, 2016|language=en-US|access-date=April 4, 2016}} Jackson was a five-star recruit and was regarded as one of the top players in the 2016 high school class.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Josh-Jackson-140396 |title=Rivals |website=Sports.yahoo.com |access-date=April 6, 2016}}{{cite web |title=Josh Jackson - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/170377 |access-date=April 6, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web |title=Josh Jackson, Prolific Prep SF - Scout |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/6594421n-josh-jackson |access-date=April 6, 2016 |website=Scouthoops.scout.com |archive-date=May 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150506122709/http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/6594421n-josh-jackson |url-status=dead }} He was ranked number one in the 2016 class by both [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]], while [[ESPN]] ranked him at number two behind only [[Harry Giles III|Harry Giles]]. [[247Sports.com]] ranked him both as the top-rated player in the 2016 class along with giving him a 102 rating, the highest rating ever given to a recruit by the website.{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Why-Kansas-signee-Josh-Jackson-is-so-special-45034992|title=Why Kansas signee Josh Jackson is so special|last=Meyer|first=Jerry|date=April 27, 2016|website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]|access-date=June 13, 2017}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2016}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Josh Jackson | position = G/F | hometown = [[Southfield, MI]] | highschool = [[Prolific Prep]] | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 195 | 40 = | commitdate = April 11, 2016 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | rivals ref title = https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/1409 | scout ref title = http://www.scout.com/player/173462-josh-jackson | espn ref title = http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/170377/josh-jackson | rivals overall = 1 | scout overall = 1 | espn overall = 2 }} ==College career== On April 11, 2016, Jackson [[tweeted]] that he would be attending the [[University of Kansas]] in [[Lawrence, Kansas]] to play basketball, picking KU over Michigan State and Arizona.{{cite news |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=April 11, 2016 |title=No. 1 recruit Josh Jackson commits to KU basketball |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article71267547.html |newspaper=[[The Kansas City Star|Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=April 13, 2016 }}{{cite tweet|number=719684761216638976|user=j_josh11|title=Next year I will be attending Kansas University 💙❤️ #RCJH |date=April 11, 2016}} During his only season at Kansas, Jackson showcased his all-around play between scoring, rebounding, play-making and defending. Although he started as a power forward for the Jayhawks, not Jackson's normal positions of both small forward or shooting guard, he still recorded 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.1 blocks per game with the team in his freshman season.{{Cite news |last=Norlander |first=Matt |date=April 17, 2017 |title=Kansas freshman Josh Jackson is finally off to the NBA Draft and could be No. 1 pick |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kansas-freshman-josh-jackson-is-finally-off-to-the-nba-draft-and-could-be-no-1-pick/ |access-date=October 5, 2024 |work=[[CBS Sports]]}} As a result of his efforts, he was named as an All-[[Big 12]] First Team member, the Big 12 Freshman of the Year, was named as a second-team All-American according to Sporting News, and was also considered a third-team All-American according to the Associated Press and National Association of Basketball Coaches. On April 17, 2017, Jackson officially declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] and hired former [[Chicago Bulls]] point guard [[B. J. Armstrong]] as his agent, officially forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |date=April 17, 2017 |title=Josh Jackson Declares for 2017 NBA Draft, Signs with an Agent |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2697548-josh-jackson-declares-for-2017-nba-draft-signs-with-an-agent |access-date=2025-08-10 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2017–2019)=== ==== 2017–18 season ==== On June 22, 2017, Jackson was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the fourth pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]], being their second straight selection at pick #4 after [[Dragan Bender]]. After he was drafted 4th by Phoenix, it was reported that Jackson had cancelled his workout with the [[Boston Celtics]], who held the 3rd pick after trading the #1 pick to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], just as the Celtics management and staff were midway to [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]] to meet him, something that reportedly angered Celtics general manager [[Danny Ainge]], although Ainge denied that it factored into his decision to not draft Jackson.{{Cite news |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=June 23, 2017 |title=Danny Ainge: Tried not to overreact to canceled workout, but I was mad |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19713510 |access-date=June 23, 2017 |work=[[ESPN]]}} When questioned on it, [[Ryan McDonough (NBA executive)|Ryan McDonough]], the general manager of the Suns, did not deny any collusion between the Suns and Jackson's representatives to dissuade the Celtics from drafting Jackson.{{Cite news |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/06/23/boston-celtics-phoenix-suns-danny-ainge/425486001/ |title=Did Suns keep Josh Jackson away from Celtics? |last=Bordow |first=Scott |date=June 23, 2017 |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=June 23, 2017}} However, Jackson attributed the situation to nothing more than poor timing and an inability to reschedule for a more proper date.{{Cite news |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2717715-suns-gm-ryan-mcdonough-says-team-played-by-the-rules-with-josh-jackson |title=Suns GM Ryan McDonough Says Team 'Played by the Rules' with Josh Jackson |last=Chiari |first=Mike |date=June 24, 2017 |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=June 27, 2017}} Jackson would sign his rookie scale contract on July 3, 2017.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-josh-jackson |title=Suns Sign Josh Jackson |date=July 3, 2017 |website=[[Phoenix Suns]] |access-date=July 3, 2017}} During the [[2017 NBA Summer League]], Jackson recorded averages of 17.4 points, a team high 9.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks per game at 35.0 minutes per game in the five games (out of the team's six total) he played there, which earned him All-Summer League First Team honors alongside [[Lonzo Ball]], [[Dennis Smith Jr.]], [[John Collins (basketball)|John Collins]] and [[Caleb Swanigan]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/josh-jackson-named-first-team-all-summer-league |title=Josh Jackson Named to All-NBA Summer League First Team |last=Cunningham |first=Cody |date=July 17, 2017 |website=[[Phoenix Suns]] |access-date=July 18, 2017}} Jackson made his NBA debut as starting power forward for the Suns on October 18, 2017. During the third game of the season, Jackson made an inappropriate, menacing gesture with his hand towards the fans of the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], which would result in him being fined $35,000 on October 24, 2017. He would start for the Suns at power forward before returning to his more natural small forward position (albeit off the bench) on October 23, 2017, in a win against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On November 29, 2017, Jackson scored a then season-high 20 points in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/reggie-jackson-scores-23-points-pistons-rout-suns-51474773 |title=Reggie Jackson Scores 23, Pistons Rout Suns 131-107 |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |date= November 29, 2017 |access-date= November 29, 2017 |last=Hogg |first=Dave}} Jackson would be put back into a starting position on December 7 at shooting guard after [[Devin Booker]]'s injury the previous game against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2017/12/7/16747380/josh-jackson-will-start-for-devin-booker-vs-washington-wizards-phoenix-suns-injury-update-lineup|title=Josh Jackson will start for Devin Booker vs. Wizards|date=December 7, 2017}} Jackson recorded his first double-double of his professional career on January 7, 2018, with 17 points, and season highs of 10 rebounds and 5 assists in a 114–100 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. After missing their next game against the [[Houston Rockets]] due to a strained right hip, he returned to the starting lineup as a small forward on January 14, recording a new career-high 21 points in a blowout loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He tied that career high on January 31 in a 102–88 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]] before putting up a new season high with 23 points on February 4 in a 115–110 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite news |last=Bonnell |first=Rick |date=February 4, 2018 |title=Kemba Walker sets Charlotte Hornets record for 3s in road win at Phoenix |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/charlotte-hornets/article198380544.html |access-date=October 5, 2024 |work=Charlotte Observer}} On his 21st birthday, Jackson would have his best all-around game in his rookie season with 20 points, 7 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal and a season-high 4 blocks in a 123–113 loss on the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He would break the previous season high in points with 29 scored on February 28 in a 110–102 win against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. On [[St. Patrick's Day]], Jackson would break that career high with the first 30-point game of his professional career with 36 points scored while coming off the bench in a 124–109 loss against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On March 20, 2018, he would record a double-double of 15 points and a career-high 11 rebounds in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. On May 22, 2018, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite news|title=Donovan Mitchell, Ben Simmons lead 2017-18 NBA All-Rookie first team|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/05/22/all-rookie-teams-release-2017-18-season|access-date=May 22, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=May 22, 2018}} ==== 2018–19 season ==== Before being named an NBA All-Rookie Second Team member, Jackson was the team's representative for the 2018 NBA Draft Lottery; the Suns won the #1 pick for the first time in franchise history on May 15, 2018.[https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article211224274.html The Kansas City Star] (subscription required) He later joined the top pick, [[Deandre Ayton]], and the Suns' other rookies and young players for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]]. During the entire pre-season, Jackson was forced into the role of the leading shooting guard, trying to replicate the role of [[Devin Booker]], who was out at the time due to finger surgery. In the season debut on October 17, 2018, Jackson returned to the bench for the team, as he recorded 18 points on 7-of-11 shooting, including 3-of-4 three-point shooting, in a 121–100 blowout win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20181017/DALPHX#/boxscore |title=Archived copy |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 18, 2018 |archive-date=October 18, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181018082913/https://www.nba.com/games/20181017/DALPHX#/boxscore |url-status=dead }} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2020)=== On July 7, 2019, the Suns traded Jackson to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-josh-jackson-de-anthony-melton-and-two-future-second-round-draft-picks-from-suns-190707|title=Grizzlies acquire Josh Jackson, De'anthony Melton and two future second round draft picks from Suns|date=July 7, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}} On September 27, the Grizzlies assigned him to the [[Memphis Hustle]], their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, for the start of the season.[https://twitter.com/ShamsCharania/status/1177615661406785542 Tweet] Jackson played in 26 games for the Hustle before being called up by the Grizzlies, averaging 20.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 1.4 blocks and 1.3 steals per game was named Midseason All-NBA G League for the Western Conference.{{cite web|url=http://www.desototimes.com/sports/four-hustle-players-on-g-league-midseason-team/article_d819a24c-4c50-11ea-96c9-f7e7fd313fa1.html|title=Four Hustle players on G League midseason team|first=Bob|last=Bakken|work=DeSoto Times-Tribune|date=February 10, 2020|access-date=February 12, 2020}} ===Detroit Pistons (2020–2022)=== On December 1, 2020, Jackson signed with his hometown team, the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agents-mason-plumlee-jahlil-okafor-josh-jackson-and-deividas-sirvydis |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Free Agents Mason Plumlee, Jahlil Okafor, Josh Jackson and Deividas Sirvydis |website=NBA.com |date=December 1, 2020 |access-date=December 1, 2020}} He made his debut for the team on December 23, logging 19 points and six rebounds in a 101–111 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Dave |date=December 24, 2020 |title=BEASLEY, TOWNS LEAD T-WOLVES RALLY PAST PISTONS 111-101 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000018 |access-date=January 24, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On April 1, 2021, Jackson scored a season-high 31 points, alongside four assists, in a 120–91 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |last=Hogg |first=Dave |date=April 1, 2021 |title=JACKSON HAS SEASON-HIGH 31 AS PISTONS ROUT WIZARDS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000179 |access-date=January 24, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He ended the 2020–21 season averaging a career-high 13.4 points per game. On January 3, 2022, Jackson scored a season-high 24 points, alongside five rebounds, in a 115–106 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |last=Megargee |first=Steve |date=January 3, 2022 |title=PISTONS WIN 115-106 TO SNAP BUCKS' 6-GAME WINNING STREAK |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100556 |access-date=January 24, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===Sacramento Kings (2022)=== On February 10, 2022, Jackson and [[Trey Lyles]] were acquired by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a four-team trade that sent [[Marvin Bagley III]] to the Pistons.{{cite web |last=Nicholson |first=Nikki |date=February 10, 2022 |title=Kings Acquire Donte DiVincenzo, Josh Jackson and Trey Lyles in Four-Team Deal |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-donte-divincenzo-josh-jackson-and-trey-lyles-four-team-deal |access-date=February 10, 2022 |website=nba.com}} The move reunited Jackson with former Suns teammates [[Richaun Holmes]] and [[Alex Len]]. On August 31, 2022, Jackson signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |last=Beloso |first=M. |date=August 31, 2022 |title=RAPTORS SIGN JACKSON |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-jackson |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} He was waived on October 14.{{cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |date=October 14, 2022 |title=Toronto Raptors Waive Former 4th Overall Pick |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/toronto-raptors-waive-former-fourth-overall-pick-josh-jackson |access-date=October 19, 2022 Here's why that's a big deal. |last=Sykes |first=Michael D. |date=August 8, 2017 |work=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=November 19, 2017}} ===Vandalism case=== On February 2, 2017, it was reported by the [[Kansas City Star]] that Jackson and Kansas teammate [[LaGerald Vick]] were persons of interest in a vandalism case that had occurred the previous December outside a bar in [[Lawrence, Kansas|Lawrence]].{{Cite news |last1=Bauer |first1=Laura |last2=Williams |first2=Mará Rose |name-list-style=and |date=February 2, 2017 |title=KU players Josh Jackson, Lagerald Vick are persons of interest in vandalism investigation |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article130423344.html |access-date=October 5, 2024 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]]}} It was alleged that Jackson and Vick had damaged the car of McKenzie Calvert, a KU women's basketball player and Vick's ex-girlfriend.{{Cite news |url=https://apnews.com/6b919e2c4c004a8c833b50a6376e5cf5/affidavit-josh-jackson-threatened-beat-womens-player |title=Affidavit: Josh Jackson threatened to 'beat' woman |last=Voigt |first=Kurt |date=March 17, 2017 |work=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=June 12, 2017}} She told police that during the incident outside the bar, Jackson yelled "for her to get out of the car and that he would beat her ass” prior to damaging her car. Following the investigation by police, Jackson was charged with one count of misdemeanor criminal damage to property and was scheduled to be arraigned on April 12.{{Cite news |last1=Bauer |first1=Laura |last2=Williams |first2=Mará Rose |name-list-style=and |date=February 24, 2017 |title=KU basketball star Josh Jackson won't miss games after misdemeanor property damage charge |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article134735694.html |access-date=October 5, 2024 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]]}} Following the announcement of the charges, Jackson released a statement apologizing for his role in the incident and offered to pay for damages. Following Jackson's charges, KU basketball coach [[Bill Self]] stated that Jackson had been disciplined internally by the administration but would not be suspended for any games due to his actions in the incident. After pleading not guilty to the vandalism charges, Jackson filed for a diversion agreement in [[Douglas County, Kansas|Douglas County]] Court which would last 12 months.{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article152020052.html |title=Former KU player Josh Jackson must apologize, attend anger management as part of diversion agreement |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=May 22, 2017 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=June 12, 2017}} As a part of the agreement, Jackson agreed to complete an anger management course, complete community service, abstain from alcohol and drug use during the diversion period, obtain substance abuse evaluation and write a letter of apology to the victims. He also agreed to pay $250 in restitution, $158 to the court and $150 for the cost of diversion. Although Jackson originally pleaded guilty, as a part of the diversion agreement he signed a stipulation of facts matching witness accounts of his actions during the incident. Following the successful completion of the diversion program, Jackson's case would be dismissed by the Douglas County Court. When asked about his progress during an interview on June 13, Jackson told reporters that he was nearly finished with the anger management course and that he had learned from his mistake.{{Cite news|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article156265314.html|title=Josh Jackson says he's 'learned from the mistake' with help from anger management class|last=Newell|first=Jesse|date=June 14, 2017|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|access-date=June 15, 2017}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.lakersnation.com/lakers-workout-kansas-josh-jackson-video-interview/2017/06/13/|title=Josh Jackson's Interview With The L.A. Media After His Workout (Video & Transcript)|last=Winters|first=Serena|date=June 13, 2017|website=Lakers Nation|access-date=June 15, 2017|quote=There is truth to that.
